source_inspiration: Base leakage case: secret-dependent table lookup maps different secret values to attacker-monitored cache sets.
Constant-time access mitigation for table lookup: access all candidate locations regardless of the secret.
Random padding mitigation for table lookup: add random extra memory accesses, but keep the original secret-dependent access.
Cache partitioning-style mitigation for table lookup: attacker monitors sets 0-3, while secret-dependent victim accesses are mapped to sets 4-7.
Base leakage case: table-driven code touches multiple secret-dependent table entries, creating a wider cache footprint.
Constant-time mitigation for multi-table lookup: touch all candidate table footprints in a fixed order regardless of the real secret.
Base leakage case: a secret-dependent branch touches one of two code/data regions, leaking the branch direction.
Balanced-footprint mitigation for secret-dependent branch: touch both branch regions in a fixed order regardless of which branch is logically selected.
Base leakage case: the number of memory locations touched depends on secret + 1.
Fixed-count mitigation for secret-dependent loop count: always touch a fixed number of locations, independent of the secret.
